expectedText:
DOMESTIC WORKER BILL OF RIGHTS — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Lee · Acme, Inc.

PURPOSE AND DECLARATION
This document sets out information about California's Domestic Worker Bill of Rights, Labor Code sections 1450 through 1455, prepared in connection with domestic work performed for Acme, Inc. by Jordan Lee in the position of Software Engineer, beginning on or about September 15, 2026. This document describes what the statute itself provides. It is not legal advice about how the statute applies to any particular person's specific work arrangement, hours, or duties.

STATUTORY TITLE AND COVERAGE
Labor Code Part 4.5, sections 1450 through 1455, is titled and may be cited as the Domestic Worker Bill of Rights. It applies to "domestic work," which the statute defines as services related to the care of persons in private households or the maintenance of private households or their premises, including occupations such as childcare providers, caregivers of people with disabilities or of sick, convalescing, or elderly persons, house cleaners, housekeepers, and maids.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "This part shall be known and may be cited as the Domestic Worker Bill of Rights."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1450 (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=1450.&lawCode=LAB)
  "“Domestic work” means services related to the care of persons in private households or maintenance of private households or their premises. Domestic work occupations include childcare providers, caregivers of people with disabilities, sick, convalescing, or elderly persons, house cleaners, housekeepers, maids, and other household occupations."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1451(a)(1) (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=1451.&lawCode=LAB)
  Known gap: Section 1451(a)(2) also states that domestic work does not include care of persons in facilities providing board or lodging in addition to medical, nursing, convalescent, aged, or child care, including residential care facilities for the elderly; that facility-based exclusion is not separately quoted here and this document does not independently verify how it applies to any specific facility. This document also does not address Labor Code section 1452 (a Governor's advisory committee provision) or section 1455 (a Division of Labor Standards Enforcement outreach and education program), which this document confirmed exist in the same Part but which do not themselves create worker entitlements.

DEFINITION OF PERSONAL ATTENDANT
Within the domestic work category, the statute separately defines "personal attendant." A personal attendant is any person employed by a private householder, or by a third-party employer recognized in the health care industry to work in a private household, to supervise, feed, or dress a child, or a person who by reason of advanced age, physical disability, or mental deficiency needs supervision. The statute states that personal attendant status applies only when no significant amount of other work is required, and it defines "no significant amount of work" as work other than supervising, feeding, or dressing that does not exceed 20 percent of the total weekly hours worked.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "“Personal attendant” means any person employed by a private householder or by any third-party employer recognized in the health care industry to work in a private household, to supervise, feed, or dress a child, or a person who by reason of advanced age, physical disability, or mental deficiency needs supervision. The status of personal attendant shall apply when no significant amount of work other than the foregoing is required. For purposes of this subdivision, “no significant amount of work” means work other than the foregoing did not exceed 20 percent of the total weekly hours worked."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1451(d) (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=1451.&lawCode=LAB)
  Known gap: This clause draws on a single statutory subsection, section 1451(d), so it is not a claim independently confirmed by more than one source. This document does not address how the 20-percent threshold is calculated or documented in practice, or how disputes over whether it is met would be resolved.

DOMESTIC WORK EMPLOYEE STATUS AND STATUTORY EXCLUSIONS
The statute defines a "domestic work employee" as an individual who performs domestic work, a category that includes both live-in domestic work employees and personal attendants. The statute then excludes several categories of people from that definition, including any person who performs services through the In-Home Supportive Services program under specified Welfare and Institutions Code provisions, and any person who is the parent, grandparent, spouse, sibling, child, or legally adopted child of the domestic work employer.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "“Domestic work employee” means an individual who performs domestic work and includes live-in domestic work employees and personal attendants."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1451(b)(1) (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=1451.&lawCode=LAB)
  "Any person who is the parent, grandparent, spouse, sibling, child, or legally adopted child of the domestic work employer."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1451(b)(2)(B) (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=1451.&lawCode=LAB)
  Known gap: The two Labor Code citations in this clause -- section 1451(b)(1) and section 1451(b)(2)(A) and (B) -- are subsections of the same statutory section, 1451, and are not independent of one another as separate sources. The statute lists additional exclusion categories in section 1451(b)(2)(C) through (G) -- including certain minors employed as babysitters, casual babysitters, employees of licensed health facilities, certain regional-center-funded caregivers, and certain exempt child care providers -- that this document confirmed exist but does not separately quote or summarize here. This document does not independently verify how any of these exclusions applies to a specific working relationship.

OVERTIME FORMULA FOR PERSONAL ATTENDANTS
The statute sets a distinct overtime formula for personal attendants that differs from California's general overtime thresholds. A domestic work employee who is a personal attendant is entitled to one and one-half times the employee's regular rate of pay for hours worked over nine in a workday and for hours worked over 45 in a workweek. This differs from the general California standard, under which the regular workday and workweek are eight hours and 40 hours, with overtime due for hours worked beyond those thresholds.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "A domestic work employee who is a personal attendant shall not be employed more than nine hours in any workday or more than 45 hours in any workweek unless the employee receives one and one-half times the employee’s regular rate of pay for all hours worked over nine hours in any workday and for all hours worked more than 45 hours in the workweek."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 1454 (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=1454.&lawCode=LAB)
  "Eight hours of labor constitutes a day’s work. Any work in excess of eight hours in one workday and any work in excess of 40 hours in any one workweek and the first eight hours worked on the seventh day of work in any one workweek shall be compensated at the rate of no less than one and one-half times the regular rate of pay for an employee."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 510(a) (California Legislative Information text), California Labor Code (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=510.&lawCode=LAB)
  Known gap: This document does not address how "regular rate of pay" is calculated for a personal attendant, how the nine-hour/45-hour thresholds interact with double-time rules that apply under the general overtime statute, or whether any other wage order provisions modify these thresholds for particular personal attendants. This document also confirmed that the statute creating this Part, Labor Code sections 1450 through 1455, does not itself contain meal-break or rest-break provisions for personal attendants or other domestic work employees; meal and rest break requirements are governed by other California wage-and-hour law outside this Part, which this document does not address.

SIGNATURE AND ACKNOWLEDGMENT
By signing below, Acme, Inc. and Jordan Lee acknowledge that they have received and reviewed this information about the Domestic Worker Bill of Rights.

Employer: Acme, Inc.
Signed: ______________________ Date: September 1, 2026

Domestic Worker: Jordan Lee
Signed: ______________________ Date: September 1, 2026

Executed at Oakland, California.
